analysis.title: Structured strategies to navigate volatility in 2027
key_insights: UBS CIO says investors should prepare for volatility in 2027 rather than try to predict or avoid every setback, and should stay invested while taking risk more thoughtfully.
Investors should keep diversified core equity exposure and consider structured strategies to manage how they participate.
UBS base case is resilient growth, rising corporate earnings, rising AI investment and moderating inflation, with further but more moderate equity gains.

Volatility is expected from high market expectations, concentrated equity exposure, uncertainty over AI investment returns, structurally higher interest rates, government debt and geopolitical tensions.
The 10 largest firms account for around 40% of the S&P 500, so changed assumptions about a small group of AI-linked businesses have an outsized effect on the index.
Structured strategies combine conventional investments with derivatives to create a predefined payoff. They redistribute risk and do not eliminate it.

Put warrant on an existing holding: gains on the warrant offset part of a loss if the holding falls below the exercise price. Maximum loss on the warrant is the premium, which is known in advance, and the warrant may expire worthless if the underlying stays above the exercise level.

Capital preservation strategies typically combine a zero-coupon bond with options on an equity or index. A higher preserved share lowers participation, protection generally applies only at maturity, and repayment depends on issuer credit.

Reverse convertibles combine a coupon-paying bond with a put option. Higher implied volatility raises option premiums and can support higher coupons, but gains are limited to the coupon while losses can be much larger if the underlying falls significantly.

UBS favors diversified underlyings and staggered maturities for reverse convertibles, and warns against choosing a structure on headline coupon alone. Single-stock structures add concentration and company-specific risk.

Investors should compare a structured strategy's outcomes with the conventional allocation it replaces, and a simpler route such as reducing or diversifying the position may suit some investors better.
earnings_insights: UBS forecasts 2027 earnings growth of around 15% for the S&P 500 and the Euro Stoxx 50, and 20% for MSCI Asia ex-Japan.

macro_indicators.interpretation: UBS expects earnings to support further, more moderate equity gains.
UBS expects earnings growth in Europe in line with the US.
UBS expects the strongest earnings growth in Asia ex-Japan.

trade_ideas.description: Buy a put warrant on an existing equity holding to limit losses
trade_ideas.rationale: Gains on the warrant offset part of the loss if the holding falls below the exercise price, while upside is retained.
trade_ideas.risk: The premium is lost if the underlying stays above the exercise price at expiry.

trade_ideas.description: Capital preservation structure: zero-coupon bond plus equity or index call options
trade_ideas.rationale: Preserves all or part of the initial investment at maturity while giving targeted participation in market gains.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher preservation reduces participation. An early sale may produce a loss, and repayment depends on issuer credit.

trade_ideas.description: Reverse convertible on diversified underlyings with staggered maturities for income
trade_ideas.rationale: Higher implied volatility raises option premiums and can support more attractive coupons.
trade_ideas.risk: Gains are limited to the coupon while losses can be much larger if the underlying falls significantly. Issuer credit risk and limited secondary-market liquidity also apply.

risk_factors: High market expectations after strong gains in recent years
Concentrated equity exposure, with the 10 largest firms near 40% of the S&P 500
Uncertainty over returns on AI investment
Structurally higher interest rates and government debt
Structured product risks: issuer credit exposure, limited secondary-market liquidity, embedded costs, conditional coupons and capital loss at maturity
vol_and_positioning: Higher implied volatility increases option premiums and can support higher coupons on reverse convertibles.
The 10 largest firms account for around 40% of the S&P 500, a concentration that magnifies the effect of changing assumptions about AI-linked businesses.
Hedging approach: a put warrant on an existing holding to limit losses while keeping upside, at the cost of an upfront premium.
geopolitical: Geopolitical tensions are listed as a source of likely volatility periods in 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient growth, rising earnings (about 15% S&P 500 EPS growth) and rising AI investment support further, more moderate equity gains.
tension_points.bear_case: High expectations, 40% top-10 concentration, uncertain AI investment returns, higher rates, government debt and geopolitical tensions are likely to produce volatile periods.

theme_stances.key_argument: Structured strategies can limit losses, generate income and retain measured market participation if used with diversification and an understanding of the terms.
theme_stances.evidence: remain invested while taking risk more thoughtfully
